nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences
nodes.label: Plant-based diet preferences

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What were some of the knowledge gaps observed among participants regarding sustainable food choices?
nodes.answer: Some participants were uncertain about which plant-based milk is better for the environment, indicating a knowledge gap in this area.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why did some participants prefer unprocessed plant foods like chickpeas and lentils over plant-based meat products?
nodes.answer: Some participants who didn't like the imitation aspect of plant-based meat products preferred unprocessed plant foods like chickpeas and lentils.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the predominant motive for consuming plant-based products according to participants?
nodes.answer: Participants mainly consumed plant-based products due to sustainability and environmental benefits, viewing them as advantageous for reducing the consumption of animal products.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Did participants consider plant-based meat/seafood products to be healthier than conventional meat and fish?
nodes.answer: Participants were uncertain about the health benefits of plant-based meat/seafood products compared to traditional options, with health not being a primary driver for consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What perception has been observed in previous studies regarding plant-based products and their health benefits?
nodes.answer: The perception that plant-based products are overly processed and potentially non-beneficial to health has been observed in previous studies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some animal welfare benefits associated with Cell-Based Meat (CBM) and Plant-Based Foods (PFD)?
nodes.answer: Animal welfare benefits observed in discussions about CBM and PFD include reduced animal suffering and ethical concerns related to traditional meat production.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do Swedish consumers perceive the environmental impact of plant-based products compared to conventional meat?
nodes.answer: Swedish consumers have varying views on the environmental benefits of plant-based products, with some sceptical while others see them as beneficial due to the removal of meat and fish from their diet.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why has there been a trend towards plant-based diets?
nodes.answer: The trend towards plant-based diets has been mainly driven by consumer concerns regarding animal welfare, sustainability, and climate change. Traditional animal-sourced foods have serious environmental footprints, including deforestation, greenhouse gas emissions, and water usage, leading many consumers to seek more sustainable and environmentally friendly alternatives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Eco-conscious consumerism|Plant-based diet preferences_qna_008
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some common sources of plant-based carbohydrates utilized in plant-based foods?
nodes.answer: Common sources of plant-based carbohydrates used in plant-based foods include algal, seaweeds, apples, corns, and various seeds. These sources provide carbohydrates such as agar, alginate, carrageenan, pectin, Nathan, and guard gum, which serve as promising texture modifiers, fat replacers, and animal skin and tissue simulators in plant-based food studies.
